subject.title: Npm-valid package scopes with dots/underscores cannot map to ClawHub publishers

question: Should ClawHub accept the shipped policy that publisher handles may include npm-compatible dots and underscores while package scopes must still match owners exactly?
rationale: The code now implements the requested behavior, but the issue was opened by a collaborator as an intentional ownership/security-boundary decision rather than a purely mechanical bug.

options.title: Accept shipped policy
options.body: Keep the current implementation, close this issue after maintainer acknowledgement, and track only narrower production repair follow-ups if needed.

options.title: Narrow to alias design
options.body: Leave current handle support in place but open a focused design item for first-class npm-scope-to-publisher aliases if maintainers want indirection.

options.title: Revert to slug-safe handles
options.body: Reject dotted/underscored handles and require package renames, accepting the compatibility cost for already-published npm packages.

recommendation.title: Accept shipped policy
recommendation.body: Keep the current implementation, close this issue after maintainer acknowledgement, and track only narrower production repair follow-ups if needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick authored both this issue context and the merged implementation, so he has the clearest current policy and code-path context.
